8867.t: From Proto-Indo-European *albʰós (“white”). Cognates include Latin albus (“white”), Hittite 𒀠𒉺𒀸 (alpas, “cloud”), Umbrian 𐌀𐌋𐌚𐌖 (alfu, “white”) and Middle Welsh elbid (“world”).

8858.t: From ἀλέκτωρ (ăléktōr, “cock, rooster”) + -υών (-uṓn, an obscure suffix also appearing in ἀλκυών (alkuṓn, “kingfisher”)).

8802.t: From ἀγωνίζομαι (agōnízomai, “I contend for a prize”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

8887.t: From ἄμνηστος (ắmnēstos, “forgotten, forgetful”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix), ultimately from μνάομαι (mnáomai, “remember”).

8878.t: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

8804.t: From earlier *ἀδϝεές (*adweés). By surface analysis, ἀ- (ă-, “not”) + δείδω (deídō, “to fear”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjectival suffix).

8891.t: ἀμφι- (amphi-, “amphi-, on two sides”) + βάλλω (bállō, “to throw”).

8835.t: Often cited as borrowed from Iranian, compared to Sogdian 𐼸𐼷𐼻𐼰𐼸 (kynʾk /⁠kīnak, kēnak⁠/, “sword”), though this etymology is disputed.

8879.t: From ἀ- (a-, not, without) + μέλω (mélō, “to care”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjective suffix).

8811.t: From ἀ- (a-, “un”) + διάλυτος (diálutos, “that may be dissolved, loosened”)

8833.t: ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + κατεργάζομαι (katergázomai, “to effect by labor, achieve”) + -τος (-tos, “adjectival suffix”).

8874.t: From ἀ (ă, “un-”) + μαθ- (măth-, root of μανθάνω (mănthắnō, “to learn”)) + -ία (-ĭ́ā).

8832.t: From ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + καθίστημι (kathístēmi, “to set in order”) + -τος (-tos).
